original.description: This activity investigates concepts for providing on-demand PNT services during crises by leveraging satellite communication systems. It aims to support continuity of positioning, navigation, and timing when terrestrial infrastructures fail due to natural disasters or humanitarian emergencies. The study will identify relevant use cases, define system concepts and requirements, and assess feasibility through preliminary designs. It will also demonstrate key components and functions via small-scale laboratory proof-of-concept setups. The outcome will include a mission study, roadmap, and verification report for future demonstrations. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

original.description: NAVISP-EL1-117-Resilience Techniques and Algorithms for GNSS Space Receivers in Interference, Jamming and Spoofing Conditions: Thisactivity aims to enhance the resilience of GNSS space receivers against interference, jamming, and spoofing in LEO. It will study and evaluate novel detection and mitigation techniques, including potential spin-in from terrestrial applications. The scope includesdefining standardized threats and scenarios to support future specifications for space receivers. The work involves simulations andearly prototyping of selected technologies to validate concepts. The goal is to maintain GNSS receiver performance during RFI events without monitoring or reporting interference. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop advanced and post-quantum Subscriber Identity Module (SIMs) for 5G/6G NTN. The focus is to improve user anonymity for robust non-terrestrialnetworks (NTNs) used for governmental applications which have a more urgent need for post-quantum anonymity protection than the commercial market. These SIMs shall implementsecurity improvements of the part of the primary authentication protocol which is implemented in the SIM. Additionally, the corresponding SIM provisioning infrastructure and the corenetwork responsible for the communication with the SIMs will be developed.TargetedImprovements: Enablinga European or Canadian source for robust NTN SIM (Physical Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) or Embedded UICC (eUICC)) for 5G/6G satellite constellation withhardened primary authentication protocolDescription: Current 5G Universal Subscriber Identity Modules (USIMs) to be used in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) for Satellite Communication (SATCOM) terminals lack adequate protectionagainst user tracking when assuming a quantum attacker. While 3GPP is working on the migration to post-quantum cryptography, the privacy needs in governmental NTN networks arehigher than in usual mobile networks and regulatory needs will require the full post-Quantum migration as early as 2030 for governmental communication solutions. An appropriatesolution therefore needs to be developed earlier than the 3GPP timeline foresees.The activity will design, develop and test prototypes of advanced 5G/6G USIMs integrating security improvements to the primary authentication protocol (user tracking enhancements inNTNs and anticipated regulatory requirements for post-quantum cryptography), with all components adhering to GSMA/ETSI security standards and targeting Common Criteria evaluationto prepare for future accreditation.The activity will evaluate two implementation paths to address this need: Physical Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) development, potentially as an applet on an existing smartcard platform, or Embedded UICC (eUICC) with appropriate SIM profiles for multi-provider service access. Post-Quantum Key Exchange Management (KEM) implementations on smartcards prove the technical feasibility of implementing such protocols in the UICC approach.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach.The first phase will study the implementation of post quantum security in the authentication protocol and perform a trade-off analysis between the two implementation paths. It will designand develop an initial prototype of the USIM and provisioning infrastructure compatible with standardised 3GPP interfaces between USIM and Mobile Equipment and perform the designof the security functions of the Core network solution to interoperate with the USIM. Phase 1 deliverables consist of architecture and design documents, initial documents to prepare thecertification, software prototype and adapted core network functions to interoperate with the software. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 700 kEuros.In the second phase, the activity will further develop and test the USIM components (UICC or eUICC), create the complete SIM provisioning infrastructure, and develop and test the corenetwork security functionsincluding the Subscriber Identifier De-concealing Function (SIDF) to support enhanced authentication of the USIM to the network. Phase 2 deliverables includethe adaptation of smart card including applet design and SIM printer or chip development for eUICC and refined certification preparation.During the activity, dissemination towards 3GPP standardisation shall be performed to ensure futureindustry adoption.

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop new Active Antenna Systems with high flexibility to adapt to traffic requestwith increased total capacity and limited payload complexity. Targeted Improvements:40% throughput increase;50% beamforming complexity reduction;Description: MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) has become increasingly important in the last generation of wireless networks, and Massive-MIMO (M-MIMO) is the key enabling technology of 5G networks. MIMO allows to maximise the reuse of the limited frequency resources and, in mobile networks, to mitigate the channel fading effects. The exploitation of MMIMO in the forward link of satellite systems requires large on-board active arrays which are subject of ongoing developments, however, the adoption of conventional Massive- MIMO for SatComs several technical challenges. Early approaches were based on accurate estimation of the Channel State Information (CSI), thus requiring regular reporting from the user equipment and tight control of the satellite payload radio frequency chains differential phase and amplitude error, to avoid performance degradation. The CSI update rate is even higher for Low Earth Orbiting (LEO) satellites due to the system orbital dynamic. Recent research has identified a number of key simplifications possible:- Replacing the channel state information with the user location information;- Converting the MIMO precoding into beam steering;- Making use on-board of Fast Fourier Transform beamforming and beam switching;- Approximating the Np-hard Radio Resource Management (RRM) with a linear complexity fast algorithm. and such pragmatic M-MIMO approach is showing excellent performance in non-uniform traffic scenarios with different distributions of the users.In this activity, pragmatic M-MIMO solutions will be further developed and applied to 5G and 6G via satellite. A scaled demonstrator, including a representative transmit active array with associated beamforming network, will be manufactured and tested with associated RRM processing, in order to verify the beamforming and RRM approach and associated advantages as compared to conventional MIMO schemes. The activity shall also estimate the Radio Access Network (RAN) implementation complexity.
